page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for high-concurrency enterprise workloads. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 processors built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 90 physical cores and 180 vCPUs via multithreading. It includes 720 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per segment. Vector execution capabilities feature AVX-512 support, including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results highlight substantial parallel compute throughput. The instance reaches a top-tier multi-core score in stress-ng and Geekbench, alongside elevated scores in Clang software compilation, PassMark encryption, and ray tracing. Memory throughput exhibits strong performance with uncached read speeds exceeding 356 GB/s and large-block write speeds of 169.03 GB/s. Memory-bound operations such as Redis SET achieve over 211 million operations per second. While single-thread decompression and gzip compression score within average-to-strong bands, its multithreaded capacity handles large language model inference prompts and text generation efficiently on 7B and 70B parameter models without dedicated accelerators.

The c3d-standard-180 does not bundle discrete GPUs or local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent storage and external network connectivity require network-attached block devices and allocated external IP addresses. Because of its large scale and 180 vCPUs, it is positioned for consolidated workloads where high thread density and heavy memory throughput eliminate distributed overhead. It delivers strong qualitative resource efficiency for high-scale microservices, enterprise relational databases, distributed caching, massive software build pipelines, and multithreaded batch processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 180 vCPUs across 90 dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 physical cores and 720 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates AVX-512 vector acceleration, including VNNI and BF16 instruction sets, while maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier multithreaded compute and memory throughput, highlighted by high Geekbench compilation scores, passmark encryption capabilities, and fast prompt processing for large language models. The instance lacks integrated GPUs and local storage drives, relying on network-attached storage architectures. Given its dense compute profile and high memory bandwidth, the instance is well suited for CPU-intensive parallel processing, Redis in-memory caching tiers, large database deployments, CI/CD compilation tasks, and enterprise application hosting.
